NOVEL-AND-FEASIBLE IDEATION:

STEP 1 — INVENT THE OBSERVABLE:
Standard practice tracks instantaneous pressure and flow rate at discrete points. My observable is the pressure wave propagation velocity variation, which indicates changes in the effective bulk modulus of the water-column system and provides early warning of column separation conditions before pressure drops occur.

STEP 2 — MAKE THE IMPLEMENTATION BORING:
The observable is calculated from existing pressure transducers at known distances using time-domain cross-correlation analysis, requiring only additional processing of existing data streams.

NOVELTY STATEMENT:
Standard practice tracks pressure and flow magnitude at specific points, while my observable tracks the pressure wave propagation velocity throughout the system. This is a genuine departure because wave velocity is sensitive to the presence of vapor cavitation precursors (dissolved gas liberation) before actual column separation occurs, providing a leading indicator rather than a failure consequence.

PHYSICS CHECK:
The governing relation is c = √(K/ρ_eff), where c is wave velocity, K is bulk modulus of water, and ρ_eff is effective density. For water at 20°C, c ≈ 1400 m/s. A 5% decrease in c (to 1330 m/s) indicates sufficient gas liberation to potentially cause column separation. This magnitude is physically meaningful as it represents the transition from single-phase to two-phase flow conditions.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL:
1. Existing pressure transducers at pump station and at least two remote locations (USER CONSTRAINT)
2. Data acquisition system capable of 100 Hz sampling (USER CONSTRAINT)
3. Processing algorithm for time-domain cross-correlation of pressure signals
4. Real-time calculation of wave velocity between transducer pairs
5. Threshold monitoring system with alarms

All components are standard industrial instrumentation. The processing algorithm would need to be developed but uses conventional signal processing techniques.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY):
- Installability: Same - uses existing pressure transducer locations
- Operability: Same - integrates with existing SCADA system
- Maintenance: Same - no additional field equipment beyond existing sensors
- Cost class: Same - only software development cost, no additional hardware
The approach imposes no additional deployment burden beyond standard practice, merely changing what is observed and calculated from existing data.

EXECUTABLE TEST:
Protocol: Initiate controlled pump trip tests at 50%, 75%, and 100% flow rates. Monitor pressure wave propagation velocity between transducer pairs.
Instruments: Existing pressure transducers, data acquisition system, processing algorithm.
Pass threshold: Wave velocity remains above 1330 m/s (within 5% of nominal) during transient.
Fail threshold: Wave velocity drops below 1330 m/s at any point during transient.
Duration: 10 tests at each flow condition.
Kill criterion: Any test showing wave velocity below threshold or exceeding 20 bar pressure (USER CONSTRAINT) fails the test.
